A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Wasserstein generalization work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures and Appendices A–F are readable, allowing additions, removals and relocated material to be distinguished.

before.justification: v1 Figure 1 reports original results from 500 synthetic logistic-regression instances. Section 3 describes the experiment and estimates how frequently the generalization bound holds.

after.justification: v2 removes that experiment without relocating it to the appendices. Its linear-model examples, bounds and remaining diagrams are theoretical; no original empirical outcomes are reported.

M1.justification: The standard Wasserstein robust objective and its double entropic regularization remain unchanged. The additions concern guarantees and assumptions, rather than new training algorithms, architectures or inference procedures.

E1.justification: v2 removes the synthetic classification experiment, eliminating the paper's entire empirical task coverage. The new linear and logistic regression analysis in Section 3.2 is mathematical, not evaluation on additional data.

E2.justification: Neither version reports an empirical comparison against competing methods. v1 Figure 1 measures whether a bound holds for robust logistic regression; the additional literature comparisons in v2 are theoretical.

E3.justification: The single illustrative evaluation protocol is removed: synthetic problems with n = 100 and d = 5, varying robustness radius, and population-risk estimation using 100,000 samples. No replacement experimental protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: v2 removes the radius-sensitivity analysis showing how the frequency of satisfying the generalization bound changes with rho. No new empirical ablations, robustness tests or error analyses replace it.

E5.justification: The disclosure of 500 generated problem instances and the associated frequency-based probability estimation disappears with the experiment. Neither version reports empirical confidence intervals, seed lists or significance tests.

E6.justification: The sole empirical result curve is removed. v1 Figure 1 shows the observed frequency of satisfying the bound increasing toward one as the radius grows; v2 reports no corresponding observations or replacement empirical results.

T1.justification: v2 adds excess-risk bounds and proofs, explicit linear/logistic-model constants, and empirical-degeneracy propositions. It adds finite Dudley entropy to Assumption 2.1 and strict feasibility to Proposition B.2. Generalization statements gain explicit sample-size conditions and larger-radius extensions, while the intermediate critical-radius threshold changes from one-half to one-quarter.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow claims covering all practical situations to broad coverage under stated compactness and complexity conditions. They also introduce excess-risk control and recovery of existing linear-model bounds as additional central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 adds substantive applicability qualifications concerning compact support, truncation, finite entropy and uncertain extension to nonparametric losses. v2 also discusses limitations of regularized excess-risk control and extends the existing degeneracy interpretation to claimed empirical-risk saturation.

D1.justification: v2 removes the experimental setup description, including the use of an l1 transport cost, a Laplace reference distribution and Monte Carlo population-risk approximation. No replacement implementation or resource-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: Five cited works are added, expanding discussion of 0-1 losses, nonparametric and non-Wasserstein robustness, and duality. Section 3.2 strengthens comparison with the already-cited Regularization via Mass Transportation. The main positioning relative to Azizian, Iutzeler and Malick remains.

P1.justification: The main narrative is extensively reorganized: the detailed proof walkthrough becomes a shorter sketch, slope arguments move into Appendix E.1, and the standalone constants discussion is redistributed. The abstract, contributions and section organization are substantially revised.

P2.justification: The document adopts different typography, title formatting, spacing and page composition throughout. The empirical Figure 1 is deleted; the maximal-radius diagram becomes Figure 1, while the slope diagram moves from the main text to Appendix E.1 as Figure 2.

improvement.justification: Explicit entropy assumptions, applicability qualifications and added excess-risk analysis improve precision and usefulness, while the empirical illustration is lost. However, new Proposition F.1 applies Theorem E.1's robust-risk comparison at rho >= rho_crit + alpha/sqrt(n), outside its stated range rho <= rho_crit/4 - beta/sqrt(n). This unresolved gap in a newly added proof prevents a reliable net quality judgment.
